questions.question: During a vehicle inspection test about oil, which of these do you NOT need to do?

options.text: Point out where the dipstick is.
Show that the oil level is safe.
Show that the oil level is above the refill mark.
Show that the oil level is below the refill mark.

questions.correctAnswerText: Show that the oil level is below the refill mark.
questions.explanation: During a vehicle inspection test, you must point out where the dipstick is, show that the oil level is safe, and show that the oil level is above the refill mark.

questions.question: If your brakes lose hydraulic pressure, which of these should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: If your brakes lose hydraulic pressure, downshift, pump the brakes, and use the parking brake. Look for a safe escape route, such as an escape ramp, open field, or side street.

questions.question: When can you refuel a bus with passengers on board?

options.text: Only if it is absolutely necessary.
Yes, if passengers are told in advance and you are in a closed building.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only if it is absolutely necessary.
questions.explanation: Do not refuel a bus with passengers on board unless it is absolutely necessary. Never refuel a bus inside a closed building while passengers are on board.

questions.question: When driving, what should you do with turn signals?

options.text: Hide your intentions from other drivers.
Use them only when other vehicles are near.
Do not use them in construction zones.
Always use them to tell others what you plan to do.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always use them to tell others what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Tell other drivers what you plan to do. Signal before you turn or change lanes, even if no other vehicles are nearby.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, what should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: When facing an aggressive driver, get out of their way. Do not provoke them by making eye contact, racing, or blocking their path. Ignore any angry gestures.

questions.question: When alley docking, what should you do first?

options.text: Position your vehicle directly in front of the alley.
Back up directly in front of the alley.
Stop next to the edge of the alley.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop next to the edge of the alley.
questions.explanation: Pull past the alley and stop your vehicle next to its outer edge. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley parking area. Park in a straight line within the space.

questions.question: What happens to shaded areas of a road in winter?

options.text: They are blocked from moisture, so they cannot freeze.
They stay slippery after ice melts on other parts of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They stay slippery after ice melts on other parts of the road.
questions.explanation: Shaded areas get less sun and warm up slowly. They stay icy and slippery after ice melts on other parts of the road.

questions.question: If there are two left turn lanes at an intersection, which lane should you use?
questions.explanation: You may need to swing right to make a safe left turn. Always start your turn in the rightmost left turn lane when two are available.

questions.question: When should you turn off your turn signal?

options.text: In the middle of the turn

questions.explanation: Signal early and keep the signal on while turning or changing lanes. Turn off your signal once the turn or lane change is complete.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT a turn signal rule?

options.text: Keep the signal on during the turn.
Turn off your signal after the turn is complete.
Only signal if another vehicle is close.

questions.correctAnswerText: Only signal if another vehicle is close.
questions.explanation: Always signal before turning or changing lanes. Start signaling early and keep it on during the turn. Turn off the signal when the turn or lane change is done.

questions.question: Poisonous fumes can enter the cab because of:

options.text: Using the wrong type of fuel.
Not enough oil in the engine.
Tires that are not filled enough.

questions.explanation: A broken exhaust system is very dangerous. Poisonous fumes can enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: To change lanes, you should:
questions.explanation: Always change lanes slowly and smoothly. This gives other drivers time to move out of your way or honk to alert you. Always use your signal when changing lanes.

questions.question: Carry-on luggage should be:

options.text: Secured so the driver can move freely and easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: Secured so the driver can move freely and easily.
questions.explanation: On a bus, all baggage must be stored so the driver can move freely, passengers can exit through any window or door in an emergency, and items cannot fall or shift and hurt riders.

questions.question: Off-ramps:

options.text: Should not be used by trucks.
Should be used only if following another vehicle.

questions.explanation: Freeway on- and off-ramps have slopes and curves that can be dangerous for trucks. Speed limits on ramps are safe for cars but may be too fast for large or heavily-loaded vehicles.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, you will be asked to:

options.text: Explain what you are inspecting and why.
Guess the weight of a load on a trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Explain what you are inspecting and why.
questions.explanation: During the vehicle inspection test, you will do a complete inspection of your vehicle. You must explain what you are inspecting and why.

questions.question: Driving in extremely hot weather:

options.text: Requires you to remove oil from the engine.

questions.explanation: In extremely hot weather, tire pressure can rise to dangerous levels because air expands in heat. Make sure your engine has enough oil and coolant to prevent overheating.

questions.question: When driving through a work zone, you should:
questions.explanation: In work zones, follow posted speed limits. Slow down if road or weather conditions are poor. Slow down even more if workers are near the road.

questions.question: Exiting your vehicle incorrectly during the basic vehicle control skills test will result in:

options.text: Automatic failure of the basic vehicle control skills test.
An extra point against your score.

questions.correctAnswerText: Automatic failure of the basic vehicle control skills test.
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. If your vehicle is a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly may result in automatic failure of the test.

questions.question: When traveling long distances, you should:
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on a long trip, take a break after every 100 miles or two hours of driving. Driving through the night or when you would normally be asleep increases the risk of fatigue.

questions.question: When entering traffic on an expressway during the skills test, you should:

options.text: Cut off other drivers if needed.

questions.explanation: During the on-road driving skills test, if you enter an expressway, check traffic first. Use proper signals and merge smoothly into the correct lane.
